title: Text shortcut remap makes plain h trigger the mapping and breaks keyboard input

status.label: Needs focused investigation
status.detail: After triggering a Keyboard Manager shortcut-to-text remap, pressing plain h reportedly retriggers the mapping and leaves keyboard input behaving as if modifiers are stuck.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve modifier state around shortcut-to-text injection
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: shortcut-to-text injection or key-up handling leaves physical and synthetic modifier state inconsistent, causing a later plain key to match; the exact failure is unconfirmed.
plan: Reproduce the exact shortcut-to-text remap and record key down/up ordering in an isolated test.
Trace source modifier release, injected text and subsequent physical key-up handling.
Correct only the demonstrated imbalance and add engine regression cases for modifier release and trigger suppression.
verification: Verify the app-specific remap repeatedly, then press plain h without retriggering it or leaving modifiers stuck; check subsequent ordinary shortcuts.

reproduce.title: Preserve modifier state around shortcut-to-text injection
prerequisites: Isolated Windows test environment with a recovery snapshot
Keyboard Manager enabled; the reporter says disabling it did not immediately restore input
setup: Create the same app-specific shortcut-to-text remap from the issue and keep a way to disable Keyboard Manager available.
steps: Focus the reported target application and trigger the remap once.
Release all keys, press plain h, and observe whether the text remap triggers again.
Try ordinary modifier shortcuts afterward and compare outside the target application.
reproduce.expected_result: The mapped text appears only for the full shortcut; plain h types h and normal shortcuts continue working.
